parts.text: a) What is the risk of ivermectin?
b) 2 ways to handle those from an endemic region for Strongy going to start immunosuppression

cohort_answer.text: a) If heavy Loa loa infection, ivermectin can precipitate an encephalopathy (mechanism unknown, believed related to high microfilaremia and rapid killing of worms - Mazzotti reaction); pre-treat with Albendazole. b) Screen with stool and serology (high sens, low specificity, positive with Wuchereria, Brugia, Onchocerca, Mansonella); Treat empirically with Albendazole or apheresis.

parts.text: a) Why is there a concern to treat with ivermectin if from a filaria endemic region (East/West Africa)?

cohort_answer.text: If patient has Loa Loa, ivermectin may precipitate encephalopathy (Loa Loa needs to be treated with DEC). Dx with serology or smear. Loa Loa: filarial nematode causing subcutaneous filariasis, vector = chrysops silacea and dimidiata (deerflies, bite during day). Takes ~5 months for larvae to become adult worms. Majority asymptomatic; symptoms - Calabar swellings and eye worm.
